lead_headline: Five restaurant leads today — Port of Subs in Littleton Square, El Pollo Loco converting Arby's in Lakewood, Reunion relocating to Platt Park, Cafecito kiosk at Colfax High, and Genna Rae Wings closing after a decade in Whittier

restaurant.blurb: 5 leads today: Port of Subs (Littleton Square), El Pollo Loco (ex-Arby's, Lakewood), Reunion Bakery (Platt Park relocation), Cafecito kiosk (Colfax High), Genna Rae Wings closure (Whittier).

liquor.blurb: Zero new applications today following Monday's 189-count surge — the 7-day total holds at 2,392 licenses, marking April's final trading days after last week's historic flood. Yesterday's batch included The Flaming Grill (891 14th St, downtown Indian fusion), Red Lotus Den (Westminster food hall targeting June), and Ultra Lounge West (Westminster karaoke venue). The 2,392-count represents an unprecedented 11,860% surge versus last week's 20 filings, confirming the event as a mass database sync or renewal wave that has fundamentally reshaped April's liquor license landscape in its closing stretch.

reputation.blurb: 9 mentions yesterday from Google News RSS lifts the 7-day count to 50 across 13 sources — up 16% from last week's 43 and extending April's late-month momentum into the final trading days. Facebook and Instagram (10 each) tie as top weekly sources, followed by Reddit and Denver Post (6 each), then Hoodline (4). Notable Monday coverage included Reddit thread on LoDo business closures, Hoodline's Marczyk Market piece, Denver Post's Re/Max headquarters departure story, and Facebook/Instagram buzz about Asian-American market support and late-night venue proposals. The 50-mention pace confirms media interest has stabilized above Q1 baselines, with social platforms driving week-over-week growth as April closes.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (1 new, 0 canceled) sustains MTD at +23 (+0.8/day) with 90-day net climbing to +121. Monday's modest gain follows Sunday's brutal −13 churn spike (4 new, 17 canceled) that wiped out much of the prior week's momentum — the 7-day total now stands at +7 net (28 new, 21 canceled), down sharply from last week's +14 and confirming April's late-month rally has stalled. Recent pattern shows Sunday's cancellation wave reversing two weeks of steady +1-2 daily gains, with MTD's +0.8/day pace now trailing YTD's +1.3/day baseline by 38%. One volatile weekend suggests April will close below March's conversion rate unless the final two days deliver outsized gains.
